documents.title: Baptism in the Holy Spirit and tongues
documents.text: Spirit baptism is an experience distinct from conversion. Tongues are normal and desirable, but they are not the only evidence of Spirit baptism. Acts 2:4 (King James Version): "And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance." Acts 8:17 (King James Version): "Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost." Acts 19:2 (King James Version): "He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost." No verdict on any person is given or implied.

documents.title: Prosperity teaching, giving and seed offerings
documents.text: God calls believers to generous, cheerful giving. God's blessing cannot be bought with a 'seed' or a pledge. Manipulation and pressure in giving are warned against. Tithing is UNDECIDED and is not taught here as a position. 2 Corinthians 9:7 (King James Version): "Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver." Acts 20:35 (King James Version): "I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive." Acts 8:20 (King James Version): "But Peter said unto him, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money." No verdict on any person is given or implied.

documents.title: Polygamy and families already in polygamous marriages
documents.text: Marriage is one man and one woman. Families already in polygamy receive pastoral care. They are not told to break up or abandon wives and children. Genesis 2:24 (King James Version): "Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh." Matthew 19:5 (King James Version): "And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh?" Mark 10:8 (King James Version): "And they twain shall be one flesh: so then they are no more twain, but one flesh." No verdict on any person is given or implied.

documents.title: Dowry and bride wealth
documents.text: Dowry is an acceptable custom when it honours both families. It must not become a sale of a person, a debt trap, or a reason to delay marriage. Genesis 2:24 (King James Version): "Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh." Exodus 22:16 (King James Version): "And if a man entice a maid that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife." Proverbs 18:22 (King James Version): "Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, and obtaineth favour of the LORD." No verdict on any person is given or implied.

documents.text: This is a developing view, under review, and not yet a settled church position. Perazim's developing view, under review: a genuinely saved person can freely and finally depart. The guide also teaches assurance of salvation and gives no verdict on any individual. Levi's wording: developing view, marked under review, with assurance and no individual verdicts.

documents.title: Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed of 381
documents.text:
We believe in one God, the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible.

And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, begotten of the Father before all worlds, Light of Light, very God of very God, begotten, not made, being of one substance with the Father; by whom all things were made; who for us men, and for our salvation, came down from heaven, and was incarnate by the Holy Ghost of the Virgin Mary, and was made man; he was crucified for us under Pontius Pilate, and suffered, and was buried, and the third day he rose again, according to the Scriptures, and ascended into heaven, and sitteth on the right hand of the Father; from thence he shall come again, with glory, to judge the quick and the dead; whose kingdom shall have no end. And in the Holy Ghost. And in the Holy Ghost, the Lord and Giver of life, who proceedeth from the Father, who with the Father and the Son together is worshiped and glorified, who spake by the prophets. In one holy catholic and apostolic Church; we acknowledge one baptism for the remission of sins; we look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the world to come. Amen.
